column1: # Short and capitalised input is variables, units and acronyms far more often
# than it is the start of a longer word.  Completing it buries the thing that
# was actually typed under a plausible-looking wrong word, which is the one
# failure mode that corrupts a document silently.
# Single letters: every one of these appears in "$x$", "let f be", "n > 0".
# Acronyms typed in capitals are deliberate, whatever their length -- including
# two letters, where a one-letter completion would otherwise be trusted and
# turn "QF" (quadratic form) into "QFT" (a different object entirely).
# ... but a real word still means itself
# ... and a one-letter, no-repair completion of a short stem is still trusted
